text.p: Pakistani police on Tuesday detained about 200 students from a Shi'ite Moslem school in Lahore, capital of Punjab province, in an apparent crackdown on sectarianism, witnesses and school administration said.

Hafiz Kazim Raza, acting principal of Jamia-al-Muntzar school, said the police raided the premises early in the morning and took away 200 senior students, five teachers and 13 other members of staff, besides seizing some licenced weapons.
Police refused to confirm the arrests, but witnesses said a police force was present around the school and only very young students were not taken away by them.

More than 100 people have been killed this year in a surge of violence in the populous central province of Punjab between rival militant groups from the majority Sunni and the minority Shi'ite sects of Islam.
Sunni groups accuse the predominantly Shi'ite neighbouring Iran of financing Shi'ite militants in Pakistan, while the Shi'ites accuse Sunni Saudi Arabia of aiding the Sunni militants.
